newsitem.title: GERMANY: Buba member sees no need to think about EMU delay.
newsitem.headline: Buba member sees no need to think about EMU delay.

text.p: Bundesbank council member Ernst Welteke said on Monday he saw no need to think about delaying European monetary union.

Asked by Reuters Financial Television whether any plans had been made for the possibility that monetary union could not start as scheduled on January 1, 1999, Welteke said: "As far as I know, there are no real plans within the Bundesbank."
He had earlier been speaking at a conference in the northern German town of Kiel.

He added in the RFTV interview: "I don't think there is any necessity to think about delay." The Bundesbank and the German finance ministry last week denied market speculation that Germany planned to seek a delay.
Welteke said he was sure financial markets would be nervous over the coming months. "But we must make our decisions and stabilise our opinions," he said.

He added that convergence of yields in European bond markets had been "impressive" last year and that perhaps markets were now seeing a "little correction," adding that he did not know if there was a trend change.
